title: ENTRYPOINT: the part that stays
summary: Split the start command into ENTRYPOINT node + CMD app.js, then run app.js, say.js and node --version from one image.

tasks.title: `greet-ep` is built with `ENTRYPOINT ["node"]` and `CMD ["app.js"]`
tasks.hint: Replace the last line of the Dockerfile with two lines: `ENTRYPOINT ["node"]` and `CMD ["app.js"]`. Save, then `docker build -t greet-ep .`

tasks.title: `ep-say`, from `greet-ep`, ran `say.js` and printed `Hello, Asha!`
tasks.hint: The command replaces only `CMD`; `node` stays in front. So give just the file: `docker run --name ep-say -e NAME=Asha greet-ep say.js`. (With `node say.js` it would run `node node say.js`.)

tasks.title: `version.txt` holds the Node version inside `greet-ep`
tasks.hint: `docker run --rm greet-ep --version` runs `node --version`. Copy what it prints (like `v24.11.0`) into `version.txt` and save.
